name: catalog-legacy-alias
goal: The workspace catalog of Electron, hosted and iOS lists no page manifest that only loads for an address at the shown revision; such a manifest stays addressable by its id, and the same id is listed at a revision where it renders

evidence: Every page manifest is a Pages card in the workspace: catalogUnit takes the category from the kind alone, while the core viewer lists as a page only what owns a +page.svelte (explorerCategory). Electron screenshot run-zuB2V2/current-pages.png starts with the Analytics redirect. Six real manifests of this checkout own only a +page.server.ts and are the former report and analytics addresses. Detail looks an entity up in the same list, so the list is the boundary, not catalogUnit. No alias field exists; the core negation is too wide to omit by (error pages, pages with no route file). Evidence: work/catalog-legacy-alias/status.md in the control directory.

Unchanged c296edb, test files frozen (frozen-tests.sha256). Desktop, real session over a two-commit Git project: bunx vitest run test/catalog-listing.test.ts, 3 failed, 1 control passed. Hosted: bunx vitest run test/hub-catalog-listing.test.ts, 3 failed, 1 control passed; the seeded cache entry is served. Browser on port 5813: playwright tests/e2e/ui-catalog-listing.spec.ts, 2 failed, 1 control passed; Pages shows 8 identities for 4. Each fails because manifests that only load for an address are listed. Before pictures taken before the assertion and inspected: before/pages-tip.png, pages-earlier.png, pages-tip-selected.png, loader-opened.png. Logs in red/.

Repair: one selector in catalogUnit.ts, used by CatalogService.list and hubCatalog. It leaves out a manifest of kind page whose every owned file at that revision is a page loader, and reads nothing else; detail, history and source keep the complete set. The hosted snapshot profile names the listing so a snapshot cached earlier is not served. Guard: the three frozen regression files in normal verification, with ordinary pages of the same title and sentence, the same identity rendered at an earlier commit, and a test that everything left out of the real registry is a Route loader to the core rule; mutants prove each rejects a heuristic, a blacklist and a lost detail.

catalogUnit.ts gains the public selector catalogListed(units, items): it leaves out a manifest of kind page whose every owned file is a page loader (+page.ts, +page.js, +page.server.ts, +page.server.js), and reads nothing else. CatalogService.list and hubCatalog().listed use it; CatalogService.entity, hubEntity, history and source keep the complete set. hubSnapshot shows listed and names the listing in its cache profile. No schema, core, renderer or native change. The guard is the three regression files: the two vitest files run in each package check, the spec in the Desktop browser suite. Registry: desktop.function.catalog-unit declares the selector; 9 reasons.

Same seven files, hashes unchanged (frozen-tests.sha256). Desktop: bunx vitest run test/catalog-listing.test.ts, 4 passed. Hosted: bunx vitest run test/hub-catalog-listing.test.ts, 4 passed. Browser on port 5813 with TAKE_SCREENSHOT=true: 3 passed. After pictures at the same checkpoints, all four inspected: after/pages-tip.png shows 4 ordinary cards and no redirect; pages-earlier.png shows the same identity as the page it was, 5 cards; pages-tip-selected.png 4 cards; loader-opened.png the redirect opened by its address. Logs in green/.

Mutants applied to module text at load time, tree untouched (guard/vite.mutant.config.ts, guard/summary.txt); unmutated control 4 of 4 in both packages. Each is rejected by the frozen files: everything listed, Desktop 3 and hosted 3 fail; by title, 3 and 2; by sentence, 2 and 1; by identity across every commit, the same-identity test in both; the core negation, 2 and 1; dropped inside catalogUnit, the opened-by-identity control in both; hosted cache profile as before, the cached-snapshot test; hosted snapshot of all items, 3; Desktop list of all items, 3. Restored source: 4 of 4 and 4 of 4.

title: A catalog snapshot saved before the listing rule is not shown as a saved copy, on the phone and in Electron as a hosted client; nothing else is invalidated.

evidence: Red on unchanged cache code, files frozen (frozen-cache-tests.sha256): hosted-copy-listing.test.ts 2 failed, 2 controls passed (the earlier copy reports.page.analytics is shown offline); ios-cache-listing.test.ts, the real Swift cache and session compiled for this Mac, 3 of 10 checks fail. Repair: RemoteCache.swift binds a kept snapshot to the rule it was listed by and lets go of one kept under another, that file only; RemoteProjectionService keeps a hosted snapshot under a key that names the listing. No pairing, Keychain, draft, media or history code changed. Green: 4 passed and 10 of 10. Native driver Debug 247, Release 225, limits 46 files. Mutants on copies: answered again, every copy purged, left on disk, rule never written, hosted key as before; each rejected (guard/cache-summary.txt). No simulator, app or device.

title: The hosted catalog and hosted client copy regressions are targets of two scenarios of their own; no runtime byte changes.

evidence: No existing scenario covered the hosted projection or the hosted client cache, and a scenario maps the tests of one package, so two were written in the current schema: hosted-catalog (packages/hub, test/hub-catalog-listing.test.ts, states hosted-listing, hosted-detail, hosted-history, hosted-cache) and hosted-client-copies (packages/desktop, test/hosted-copy-listing.test.ts, states earlier-copy, current-copy, other-copies, denial). Mapping in test/hosted-verification-scopes.ts; 13 unit bindings, both ways. The hub test changed by its import of the observing expect only (frozen-additive-hub.diff; original kept, equal to its frozen hash); nine mutants give the same outcomes as before. Declared commands through the real wrapper and validators on the working tree: both passed, 4 of 4 required states and 8 captures each, 17 and 10 matchers observed. scenarios check 18, units check 1195, explain check 20 reasons, audits, hub types, lint and format pass. Runtime and native cache files unchanged.
